true_positives.matched_candidate:
Origin check uses substring match and URL assumes trailing slash

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For `discourseUrl = "https://forum.example.com/"`, messages from `https://forum.example.co` or `https://forum.example.c` (any prefix) pass the check, so a different frame on the host page could resize the embed iframe. Compare `e.origin` against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` exactly. Separately, line 7 builds `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`, which produces a broken URL (`...comembed/best`) unless the site owner remembers to include a trailing slash in `discourseUrl`; normalize the base URL.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw-HTML post `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the post contents with no HTML/attribute escaping, and the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, which (per the new `Post#cook`) bypasses sanitization entirely. The `url` is attacker-influenced: `EmbedController#best` accepts any `embed_url` param and `TopicRetriever` only checks that the URI host equals `embeddable_host`, so the path/query are free-form. `'`, `=`, `(`, `)` are valid URI characters, so a request like `/embed/best?embed_url=http://host/real-post?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` (with a spoofed Referer) makes the job fetch the real page (query strings are ignored by most servers) and store `` in a public topic authored by the embed user. Nokogiri in `absolutize_urls` preserves the injected attribute. Escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape`/`CGI.escapeHTML` (and ideally sanitize the whole imported HTML before storing it as raw_html).

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident

The conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Ruby parses the trailing `if` as a statement modifier whose condition is the next generated ERB statement (the buffer append for the following whitespace/text), so the template happens to compile, but the order of evaluation is now dependent on how the ERB engine emits the surrounding code and will break with a syntax error if the following text segment is removed or the template compiler changes (e.g. switching Erubis/Erubi). Replace with `<%- end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
i.content can be nil for RSS items, aborting the whole feed import

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (and SimpleRSS returns nil for a missing tag), so `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is `retry: false`, a single item without content makes every hourly poll fail and nothing from the feed is ever imported. The same applies to a nil `i.title`. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with no usable body instead of raising.

postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Core import paths are untested

The specs only verify that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed`; `poll_feed` itself (SimpleRSS parsing, the `i.content` nil case, link/id fallback), `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` (protocol-relative and non-standard-port cases), and the escaping of the appended "Imported from" link are all without coverage. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` the example titled "is 404 without an embed_url" actually exercises `params.require`, which raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (HTTP 400), and the assertion is only `should_not be_success`, so the title is misleading and would not catch a regression in the status code.

Disqus import loses thread created_at/category and may crash on bad links

The thread topic was previously created with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and an optional `category`; it is now created via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title:)`, which ignores both, so all imported Disqus threads get `created_at = now` (breaking topic ordering/dates) and the `-c` option is silently gone. Also `import_remote` calls `open(url)` before any URL validation: a thread with a missing or relative `link` causes `TypeError`/`Errno::ENOENT` from `Kernel#open` and aborts the whole import rather than being skipped as the `return unless url =~ /^https?:/` guard in `TopicEmbed.import` intends.

Every unknown embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll

`perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `feed_polling_enabled` is on and the URL has no embed yet. That downloads and parses the entire RSS/Atom feed and runs `TopicEmbed.import` (SHA, Nokogiri parse, possible PostRevisor revision) for every item, before even attempting the direct HTTP fetch. Since the per-URL 60s throttle does not limit distinct URLs, a burst of requests for different (or merely query-string-varied) URLs re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed concurrently from multiple Sidekiq workers, hammering both the remote site and the database. At minimum guard the feed poll with a global short-lived lock/throttle rather than running it per embed URL.

Host-spam check still applies to imports and post errors are not checked

`PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true)` skips model validations but not `rollback_if_host_spam_detected`. Every imported post links to the embeddable host (the appended "Imported from" link plus absolutized links), so once the `embed_by_username` user (typically a fresh TL0 account) has `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (default 3) posts linking that host, `has_host_spam?` returns true, the post is rolled back, and a spam GroupMessage is sent to moderators on every subsequent import. Worse, `PostCreator#create` still returns the unsaved `@post` object, so `if post.present?` is true and `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` is attempted with a nil `post_id`, which blows up on the NOT NULL constraint. Check `post.errors.blank?`/`post.persisted?` before creating the embed, and bypass the host-spam check for system imports (or require a trusted import user).

SETNX followed by EXPIRE is not atomic; key can become permanent

`retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and then a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the worker dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the key is left with no TTL, and that embed URL is throttled forever (`setnx` will always return false), so its topic can never be retrieved for non-staff users. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (atomic) or wrap in MULTI.

Unauthenticated callers can trigger arbitrary server-side fetches and unbounded topic creation

Any request to `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a spoofed `Referer` header (the only check in `ensure_embeddable`) enqueues `RetrieveTopic`, which fetches the URL with `open-uri` and creates a new topic as the `embed_by_username` user. The only constraint is that the URI host matches `embeddable_host`; the path and query string are arbitrary, so `http://host/page?1`, `http://host/page?2`, ... each produce a distinct `TopicEmbed` and topic. The throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed on the full URL (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), so it does not limit this at all. Consequences: unbounded topic spam from the forum's own account, and server-side request amplification (open-uri also follows redirects to any host, so an open redirect on the embeddable site turns this into SSRF). Consider a global rate limit, normalizing/stripping query strings, verifying the fetched page actually references the forum, and/or requiring a successful 200 from a canonical URL.

Updating an embed whose post was deleted raises NoMethodError

In the update branch, `post = embed.post` uses the `belongs_to :post` association. `Post` includes `Trashable`, whose default scope hides trashed rows, so if a moderator deleted the imported post, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` fails on `@post.raw`. For the hourly `PollFeed` job this exception aborts the import loop for every remaining feed item (and `retry: false`), permanently breaking feed polling once any imported post is deleted. Guard against a nil/trashed post (skip or re-create).

`force: true` added to create_table drops existing data on re-run

This migration (unrelated to the embed feature) is changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, and the new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`. `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` before creating, so any environment where the table already exists (e.g. re-running migrations after a partial failure, or a schema drift) silently loses all rows. Migrations should not use `force: true`; if the goal is idempotency, guard with `unless table_exists?`.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

`absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as site-relative and rewrites it to `#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}`. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in feeds and CMS output) also start with `/`, so they are turned into `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking every such link and image in imported posts. The same bug is on line 70 for `img[src]`. Check `start_with?('//')` first and only prepend the scheme in that case, or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`align-items` mixin passes modern keywords unchanged to legacy syntaxes with a different vocabulary, and emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property

The `align-items($alignment)` mixin forwards `$alignment` verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` (2009 box spec) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 tweener spec). Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`/`center`/`baseline`/`stretch`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, which happen to overlap, but any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently produce invalid declarations for the very browsers the prefixes are meant to support. The mixin should map `flex-start`→`start` and `flex-end`→`end` for the legacy outputs. Additionally, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a property any version of IE ever implemented and only adds dead bytes to the compiled CSS.

false_positives.candidate:
PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make; description is a placeholder

The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and described only as "Test 5". The diff replaces float-based layout with flexbox and reflows `.small-action` and category badge spacing; nothing in it measurably affects rendering performance (flexbox is not faster than floats, and the header's scroll performance hint `backface-visibility: hidden` is untouched). `float: right` on `.small-action button` is ignored now that `.small-action` is a flex container

Per the flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` left on `.small-action button` no longer pushes the action button (e.g. the edit/show-all control on small-action posts) to the right edge. If those engines are considered unsupported the `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` lines should be dropped from the mixins; if they are supported, the panel needs an explicit `-webkit-box-flex`/spacer approach or the `float` should be kept as a fallback.

Injecting the literal string "refresh_token" clobbers real refresh tokens in the DB

When the parsed response lacks `refresh_token`, the helper sets `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (a placeholder string). Callers then persist this: Zoom does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` and Office365 does `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`, so the user's genuine refresh token in `credential.key` is overwritten with the literal `"refresh_token"`. Once clobbered, disabling sync (or the next normal refresh) fails permanently with invalid_grant and the user must reconnect the app. Don't mutate the parsed data; leave the field absent and let callers keep the existing stored refresh token.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses bogus computed keys and strips every field except `access_token`

`[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` do not create pattern/catch-all keys; `ZodType.toString()` returns `"[object Object]"`, so both lines define the same literal property `"[object Object]"` (the second overrides the first). The resulting schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string() })`, and since `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set the returned `data` contains only `access_token`. The comment "Assume that any property with a number is the expiry" is not implemented. Use `.passthrough()` or `z.record()`/`.catchall()` and validate the expiry explicitly.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for the new webhook endpoint or the shared OAuth helpers

The PR adds a new authenticated API route that writes third-party credentials into the database, plus two helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that are now on the token-refresh path of 10+ integrations, with zero automated tests (the author's checklist confirms this). Several of the defects in this PR — the Google key being stored as a SafeParse wrapper, the broken computed-key zod schema, the missing `prisma` import in Salesforce, the dirName-vs-slug metadata lookup — would have been caught by even a minimal unit test of each helper and a request-level test of the webhook. At minimum add tests for: secret validation, 404 paths, create-vs-update, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` output in both sync and non-sync modes.

Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication

The sync request POSTs only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as form fields with no shared secret, signature or bearer header. The self-hoster's endpoint therefore has no way to verify the request came from Cal.com, and anyone who can reach that endpoint can obtain any user's third-party access tokens simply by posting a user id. The inbound webhook (`app-credential.ts`) uses `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the outbound request should at minimum send that secret in `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` so the endpoint can authenticate the caller. The comment "Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires" also implies self-hosters are expected to edit source, which is not a viable contract. Note also the `appSlug` values are inconsistent: Zoom passes `"zoomvideo"` (directory name) while its DB slug is `"zoom"`, and MS Teams passes `"msteams"` (slug).

Webhook secret compared with `!==` and endpoint accepts any HTTP method

The shared secret is compared with a plain string `!==`, which is not constant-time; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also does not restrict `req.method` to POST, and `req.headers[...]` may be a `string[]` if the header is repeated. Additionally, if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` were ever unset the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` check happens to protect it, but the comparison itself would otherwise be `undefined !== undefined === false` and allow unauthenticated writes — worth an explicit guard.

`appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name, not by App.slug, so most apps return 404

The handler looks up the app by `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })` and then indexes `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]`. `appStoreMetadata` (from `@calcom/app-store/appStoreMetaData`, built from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by directory name — `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `larkcalendar`, `office365video` — while the DB slugs are `google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `msteams`. For all of those the lookup yields `undefined` and the webhook responds `404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"`, so the headline feature cannot sync credentials for the main calendar/video apps. Only apps whose dirName equals their slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, webex, zoho-bigin) happen to work. Look the metadata up by matching `.slug` (e.g. `Object.values(appStoreMetadata).find(m => m.slug === app.slug)`) or use the `type`/`dirName` stored on the App row.

`prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService

The new code in `getClient` calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (the import list only contains jsforce, rrule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, http-error, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This fails type-check and, at runtime, throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce service instantiation, breaking the Salesforce integration completely.

`test_basic` does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top, and the new line `time.sleep(0.1)` resolves `time.sleep` at call time through the `time` module, so it calls the patched no-op. The comment says it gives the flusher thread time to process after the drift change, but it waits zero seconds. The race it was meant to fix remains: `step.join()` immediately sets `stopped`, and if the flusher thread observes `stopped` before running `flush_segments` with the new drift, `messages` is empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails. true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

`_ensure_processes_alive` only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` — a direct subclass of `BaseProcess`, not of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`). The isinstance check is therefore always False in production, and `kill()` is never invoked. The previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a process is deemed hung (`cause == "hang"`), it is left running and a second process is started for the same shards. Two flushers then concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same Redis shards, producing duplicate segments to Kafka and racing on Redis state, while the stale processes accumulate (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per index). The same broken check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is also never called on shutdown. true_positives.matched_candidate:

In `join()`, when the deadline has passed the loop does `break`, so any processes not yet visited never reach `process.terminate()`. The inner `while` already exits immediately once the deadline has passed, so the `break` is unnecessary and only has the effect of skipping termination of the remaining processes. On a slow shutdown this leaves spawned flusher processes running after the consumer's strategy has been joined (they are daemonic, but will keep flushing until the parent actually exits).

Docstring claims one process per shard, but the default CLI setting is a single process

The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but the number of processes is `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`, and the `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1, so in the default configuration a single process handles all shards. No test covers shard-to-process assignment correctness or the multi-process restart path

`test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks process counts and that the total number of mapped shards equals 4. It does not assert that shards are disjoint across processes or balanced (e.g. process 0 -> [0, 2], process 1 -> [1, 3]), and nothing exercises `_ensure_processes_alive` restarting one of several processes (per-index restart counters, per-index healthy_since/backpressure values, killing the old process). `submit()` iterates `self.buffers.values()` and calls `get_memory_info()` on each. Every `SpansBuffer` connects to the same Redis cluster, so each call returns the memory info for all cluster nodes; with N flusher processes this issues N× the INFO round-trips per submit and sums N copies of the same used/available values (the ratio is unchanged but the work is redundant). Similarly `record_stored_segments()` is called per buffer. Querying memory info once (e.g. on a single buffer) is sufficient.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit

`CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and the INSERT/upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or lock. N concurrent first-time anonymous requests arriving while `count == deviceLimit-1` will all observe a count below the limit and all insert, so the stored device count can exceed `deviceLimit` by the degree of concurrency. Enforcing the limit in a single transaction (or with a serverlock/advisory lock) is required for the limit to be a hard cap.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache is populated before the limited insert, so a rejected device is admitted on its next request

`tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the cache entry remains for ~29 minutes. On the device's very next request `localCache.Get(key)` hits, `tagDeviceUI` returns nil, `TagDevice` returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` issues an identity. The new device limit therefore only rejects the first request from an over-limit device; a reload (which the browser/UI will naturally do) bypasses the limit entirely, and the device is never written to the DB so it isn't even counted. The cache must be set only after a successful write (or removed on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Device limit is trivially bypassed by clients that omit the X-Grafana-Device-Id header or have an unparsable address

`TagDevice` returns nil (no error) when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent and also when `network.GetIPFromAddress` fails. Since `Anonymous.Authenticate` only denies access on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, any anonymous client that simply does not send the device header (curl, scripts, API consumers, a browser with the header stripped) is authenticated regardless of the configured `device_limit`. If the limit is intended as an enforcement mechanism rather than best-effort UI accounting, requests without a device ID should be rejected when a limit is configured, or the limitation should be clearly documented.

Previously tagging ran in a detached goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout; now `TagDevice` executes inline inside `Authenticate` using the request context. For every uncached device this adds a `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ...` (full range scan on a table that can hold tens of thousands of rows when a limit is configured) plus an INSERT/UPDATE before the identity is returned, and any DB slowness now directly delays or fails anonymous page loads. The local cache mitigates this per device for ~29 minutes but not for first requests or multi-instance deployments. Limit test does not cover the update path for an existing device or the cache bypass

`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second, new device gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. It does not verify that an already-registered device can still be updated when the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` branch returning nil), that a device whose last update is older than 30 days is rejected, or that the service layer (`TagDevice`/`Authenticate`) actually denies the device on repeated requests. `ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires an `int64` argument and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now takes `db.DB` instead of `anonstore.AnonStore`. `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` makes TypeScript infer the property type as the literal `undefined` (under strictNullChecks), so consumers of `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` cannot use it as a number without a cast. false_positives.candidate:
Unauthenticated callers can trigger arbitrary server-side fetches and unbounded topic creation

Any request to `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a spoofed `Referer` header (the only check in `ensure_embeddable`) enqueues `RetrieveTopic`, which fetches the URL with `open-uri` and creates a new topic as the `embed_by_username` user. The only constraint is that the URI host matches `embeddable_host`; the path and query string are arbitrary, so `http://host/page?1`, `http://host/page?2`, ... each produce a distinct `TopicEmbed` and topic. The throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed on the full URL (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), so it does not limit this at all. Consequences: unbounded topic spam from the forum's own account, and server-side request amplification (open-uri also follows redirects to any host, so an open redirect on the embeddable site turns this into SSRF). Consider a global rate limit, normalizing/stripping query strings, verifying the fetched page actually references the forum, and/or requiring a successful 200 from a canonical URL.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

`absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as site-relative and rewrites it to `#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}`. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in feeds and CMS output) also start with `/`, so they are turned into `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking every such link and image in imported posts. The same bug is on line 70 for `img[src]`. Check `start_with?('//')` first and only prepend the scheme in that case, or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles all relative forms correctly.

Host-spam check still applies to imports and post errors are not checked

`PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true)` skips model validations but not `rollback_if_host_spam_detected`. Every imported post links to the embeddable host (the appended "Imported from" link plus absolutized links), so once the `embed_by_username` user (typically a fresh TL0 account) has `newuser_spam_host_threshold` (default 3) posts linking that host, `has_host_spam?` returns true, the post is rolled back, and a spam GroupMessage is sent to moderators on every subsequent import. Worse, `PostCreator#create` still returns the unsaved `@post` object, so `if post.present?` is true and `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id)` is attempted with a nil `post_id`, which blows up on the NOT NULL constraint. Check `post.errors.blank?`/`post.persisted?` before creating the embed, and bypass the host-spam check for system imports (or require a trusted import user).

Every unknown embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll

`perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `feed_polling_enabled` is on and the URL has no embed yet. That downloads and parses the entire RSS/Atom feed and runs `TopicEmbed.import` (SHA, Nokogiri parse, possible PostRevisor revision) for every item, before even attempting the direct HTTP fetch. Since the per-URL 60s throttle does not limit distinct URLs, a burst of requests for different (or merely query-string-varied) URLs re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed concurrently from multiple Sidekiq workers, hammering both the remote site and the database. At minimum guard the feed poll with a global short-lived lock/throttle rather than running it per embed URL.

SETNX followed by EXPIRE is not atomic; key can become permanent

`retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and then a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)`. If the worker dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the key is left with no TTL, and that embed URL is throttled forever (`setnx` will always return false), so its topic can never be retrieved for non-staff users. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (atomic) or wrap in MULTI.

`<%- end if %>` is a typo that only compiles by accident

The conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. Ruby parses the trailing `if` as a statement modifier whose condition is the next generated ERB statement (the buffer append for the following whitespace/text), so the template happens to compile, but the order of evaluation is now dependent on how the ERB engine emits the surrounding code and will break with a syntax error if the following text segment is removed or the template compiler changes (e.g. switching Erubis/Erubi). Replace with `<%- end %>`.

`force: true` added to create_table drops existing data on re-run

This migration (unrelated to the embed feature) is changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, and the new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`. `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` before creating, so any environment where the table already exists (e.g. re-running migrations after a partial failure, or a schema drift) silently loses all rows. Migrations should not use `force: true`; if the goal is idempotency, guard with `unless table_exists?`.

In the update branch, `post = embed.post` uses the `belongs_to :post` association. `Post` includes `Trashable`, whose default scope hides trashed rows, so if a moderator deleted the imported post, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` fails on `@post.raw`. The thread topic was previously created with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and an optional `category`; it is now created via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title:)`, which ignores both, so all imported Disqus threads get `created_at = now` (breaking topic ordering/dates) and the `-c` option is silently gone. Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication

The sync request POSTs only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as form fields with no shared secret, signature or bearer header. The self-hoster's endpoint therefore has no way to verify the request came from Cal.com, and anyone who can reach that endpoint can obtain any user's third-party access tokens simply by posting a user id. The inbound webhook (`app-credential.ts`) uses `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the outbound request should at minimum send that secret in `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` so the endpoint can authenticate the caller. The comment "Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires" also implies self-hosters are expected to edit source, which is not a viable contract. Note also the `appSlug` values are inconsistent: Zoom passes `"zoomvideo"` (directory name) while its DB slug is `"zoom"`, and MS Teams passes `"msteams"` (slug).

`appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name, not by App.slug, so most apps return 404

The handler looks up the app by `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })` and then indexes `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]`. `appStoreMetadata` (from `@calcom/app-store/appStoreMetaData`, built from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by directory name — `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `larkcalendar`, `office365video` — while the DB slugs are `google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `msteams`. For all of those the lookup yields `undefined` and the webhook responds `404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug"`, so the headline feature cannot sync credentials for the main calendar/video apps. Only apps whose dirName equals their slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, webex, zoho-bigin) happen to work. Look the metadata up by matching `.slug` (e.g. `Object.values(appStoreMetadata).find(m => m.slug === app.slug)`) or use the `type`/`dirName` stored on the App row.

Webhook secret compared with `!==` and endpoint accepts any HTTP method

The shared secret is compared with a plain string `!==`, which is not constant-time; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also does not restrict `req.method` to POST, and `req.headers[...]` may be a `string[]` if the header is repeated. Additionally, if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` were ever unset the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` check happens to protect it, but the comparison itself would otherwise be `undefined !== undefined === false` and allow unauthenticated writes — worth an explicit guard.

No tests for the new webhook endpoint or the shared OAuth helpers

The PR adds a new authenticated API route that writes third-party credentials into the database, plus two helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that are now on the token-refresh path of 10+ integrations, with zero automated tests (the author's checklist confirms this). Several of the defects in this PR — the Google key being stored as a SafeParse wrapper, the broken computed-key zod schema, the missing `prisma` import in Salesforce, the dirName-vs-slug metadata lookup — would have been caught by even a minimal unit test of each helper and a request-level test of the webhook. At minimum add tests for: secret validation, 404 paths, create-vs-update, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` output in both sync and non-sync modes.
